figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Liquid chromatography of the degradation residues for AFB1, ZEN, and DON by PpLac1 and AoLac2. The concentrations of these three
mycotoxins were 2 μg/mL each. (A) Liquid chromatography of the degradation for AFB1 was performed by two laccases. The elution time of AFB1
was 2.98 min. The black line represents the liquid chromatography of the AFB1 control, and the peak area was 46015. The blue line represents the
liquid chromatography of the degradation for AFB1 by the laccase PpLac1, and the peak area was 24540. The red line represents the liquid
chromatography of the degradation for AFB1 by the laccase AoLac2, and the peak area was 24100. (B) Liquid chromatography of the degradation
for ZEN was carried out by two laccases. The elution time of ZEN was 5.62 min. The black line represents the liquid chromatography of the ZEN
control, and the peak area was 3259. The blue line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation for ZEN by laccase PpLac1, and the
peak area was 1503. The red line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation for ZEN by the laccase AoLac2, and the peak area was
1346. (C) Liquid chromatography of the degradation for DON by two laccases. The elution time of DON was 0.57 min. The black line represents
the liquid chromatography of the DON control, and the peak area was 597. The blue line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation
for DON by the laccase PpLac1, and the peak area was 583. The red line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation for ZEN by the
laccase AoLac2, and the peak area was 564.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Molecular docking simulation of laccases AoLac2, Laccase 53739, and laccase PpLac1 with DON. (A) Molecular docking simulation of
AoLac2 with DON. DON formed two hydrogen bonds with the side chains of serine (Ser124) and aspartic acid (Asp233) in AoLac2. (B)
Molecular docking simulation of Laccase 53739 with DON. DON formed four hydrogen bonds with the side chains of serine (Ser33), leucine
(Leu35), glutamate (Glu142), and threonine (Thr147) in Laccase 53739. (C) Amino acid residue differences between AoLac2 and laccase 53739
near the DON binding site, where the pink sticks indicates amino acid residues of AoLac2 and the green sticks indicates amino acid residues of
Laccase 53739. (D) Molecular docking simulation of PpLac1. PpLac1 could not bind to DON.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Optimization of mycotoxin degradation parameters for AFB1 and ZEN by laccases PpLac1 and AoLac2. (A) Effect of temperature on the
degradation of PpLac1. (B) Effect of pH on the degradation of PpLac1. (C) Effect of protein concentration on the degradation of PpLac1. (D)
Effect of mediator types on the degradation of PpLac1. (E) Effect of temperature on the degradation of AoLac2. (F) Effect of pH on the
degradation of AoLac2. (G) Effect of protein concentration on the degradation of AoLac2. (H) Effect of mediator types on the degradation of
AoLac2.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 8. Liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry of the degradation products of AFB1 and ZEN. The concentration of AFB1 and ZEN was
5 μg/mL each. (A) Liquid chromatography of the AFB1 degradation product. The elution time of the product was 4.46 min. The black line
represents the liquid chromatography of the AFB1 control. The blue line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation product of AFB1
by laccase after 12 h. The red line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation product of AFB1 by laccase after 24 h. As time
increased, the peaks of the degradation product increased. (B) Mass spectrometry of AFB1. (C) Mass spectrometry of AFQ1. (D) Liquid
chromatography of the ZEN degradation product. The elution time of the product was 3.13 min. The black line represents the liquid
chromatography of the ZEN control. The blue line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation product of ZEN by laccase after 3 h.
The red line represents the liquid chromatography of the degradation product of ZEN by laccase after 6 h. As time increased, the peaks of the
degradation product increased. (E) Mass spectrometry of ZEN. (F) Mass spectrometry of 15-OH-ZEN.
